rule.description: A function defined outside src/entry.c that reads one of the theme inheritance bookkeeping flags (foreground_specified, background_specified, padding_specified, radius_specified, color_specified, text_color_specified) is resolving entry-owned theme inheritance locally instead of leaving that decision to the entry module that owns struct entry and its themes. Flag writes during configuration parsing and the unrelated thickness_specified font-metric fallback are not part of the relation.

checks.description: Reports each function defined outside src/entry.c that reads a theme inheritance bookkeeping flag in order to decide an effective theme value at that site.
checks.detected_relation: non-owner function -> local resolution of entry-owned theme inheritance
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each matching function holds one fragment of the single inheritance decision, so a conceptual change to what unset text or cursor theme fields inherit must be replicated at every fragment (and mirrored across both rendering backends, plus the parser) instead of being made in one place.

matches.evidence: The window-wide text-colour handler reads the foreground_specified flag of all six per-element themes (prompt, input, placeholder, default result, alternate result, selection) to decide, inside option parsing, which of them should have their foreground colour overwritten with the parsed value.

The per-frame HarfBuzz driver resolves themes itself before drawing: it reads foreground/background/padding/radius_specified twice each for the default result theme (which alternating rows inherit from) and twice each for the selection theme, then feeds the resolved copies into row rendering and the two-pass selected-row highlight.

The HarfBuzz input-line draw helper takes the whole entry, builds the window-level default theme locally, and reads foreground/background/padding/radius_specified on the incoming theme plus color_specified and text_color_specified on the cursor theme to resolve both inline before drawing.

The HarfBuzz themed-text draw helper gained a fallback theme parameter and reads foreground/background/padding/radius_specified on the incoming theme to fill a local resolved copy, drawing the prompt and every result row through it.

The per-frame Pango driver mirrors the HarfBuzz driver: eight flag reads across the default result and selection themes, whose resolved copies then drive row rendering and the two-pass selected-row highlight in this backend.

The Pango input-line draw helper mirrors its HarfBuzz counterpart: local window-level default theme construction, four flag reads resolving the input theme, and the two cursor flag reads resolving cursor colours inline.

The Pango themed-text draw helper gained the same fallback parameter and the same four flag reads resolving a local copy of the incoming theme, through which the prompt and all result rows of this backend are drawn.

excluded.reason: A *_specified-style conditional fallback that computes a font-metrics default for cursor thickness; theming-shaped but an unrelated rule, deliberately outside the relation and not named by the check.

excluded.symbol: assignment writes of the inheritance flags
excluded.reason: Write-side bookkeeping recording which fields the user explicitly configured predates the change and must keep working; the rule reports only reads, and the parser's own assignment targets are never matched.

excluded.symbol: any function in the owner translation unit
excluded.reason: src/entry.c owns struct entry and its themes and is the legitimate home of the inheritance decision; functions defined there are exempt by construction so the check credits only non-owner sites.
Reading the window-level root colours without an inheritance flag test is consuming a root value, not deciding a fallback; only flag-guarded resolution counts.
